title: Studio work, auditions and playing for Mae West
summary: He had dates at MGM and Fox; at an audition he won the job by not playing 'Sweet Sue' like the other bands, and also played for Mae Murray and Mae West.

bands.name: Mae Murray's New Orleans Jazz Band

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I used to play, I had -- I had all the dates in the studios --
MGM, and Atlantic, oh ah, it's a -- Fox --

-- I was pretty good there, I had a run, they liked me, pretty good (unintelligible) I furnished them good music, but one time we went out to Fox Hill, it was (unintelligible) the band to come do auditions --
So -- oh, three or four bands come out there, then (they'd call) another band would come to audition, all this in one day you know --

-- there were five bands, your band had got there before (unintelligible) and another band would come in and play, another band come in and play, yet come another bunch and the man look over there -- say, you was in the band that set in -- (inaudible). Some of the same guys.
So when they call the tops, that was me, we come in there, we play that -- one number, that's enough.
It's all right. You got the job. See every band was coming in here playing, 'Sweet Sue' --
Every band that come in there da-da-da-da-da-da-da. You know?
I played something, I forgot what I played. I didn't play no 'Sweet Sue.' Cause I knew what they was going to do; played (unintelligible) we play some nice pretty music.
Give me the job right away.
Was that -- so you played for some of the movies in those days?
Played for Mae Murray and her New Orleans jazz band.
Played for -- what's that woman's name.
Her (unintelligible) was come up some time. (Unintelligible) she was on the air --
Uah, sure, oh, how can we forget Mae West?
I played a lot of them.
So you did a big variety of music?
